binders: Ω is an arbitrary type equipped with a measurable-space structure.
μ is a measure on Ω equipped with an IsFiniteMeasure instance.
hN is a proof that 0 < N.
X is a family of real-valued functions X i : Ω → Real indexed by i : Fin N.
hypotheses: For every i : Fin N, X i belongs to L2(μ), i.e. it is strongly measurable almost everywhere and has finite L2 seminorm.
For every distinct i,j : Fin N, X i and X j are independent under μ.
For every i : Fin N, X i and X 0 are identically distributed under μ, where X 0 uses the Fin N element constructed from 0 < N.
conclusions: The variance under μ of the pointwise empirical average ω ↦ (1 / (N : Real)) · ∑ i : Fin N, X i ω equals (1 / (N : Real)) times the variance under μ of X 0.
mathematical_definitions: The empirical average is the function ω ↦ N⁻¹ ∑_{i=0}^{N-1} X_i(ω), with N interpreted as a real number.
X 0 denotes X applied to the index 0 in Fin N, whose existence follows from N > 0.
Variance is ProbabilityTheory.variance, the real value obtained from ProbabilityTheory.evariance by ENNReal.toReal.
The L2 assumption is expressed by MeasureTheory.MemLp (X i) 2 μ.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For a positive finite family of pairwise independent, identically distributed, square-integrable real-valued functions on a finite measure space, the variance of their empirical average is the variance of any one member divided by the family size N.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The measure μ is assumed finite but is not explicitly assumed to be a probability measure; this is weaker than the usual statement of the variance-of-the-mean formula and may affect how independence and variance behave.
Only pairwise independence is required, not mutual independence; pairwise independence is ordinarily sufficient for the variance calculation.
The positivity hypothesis N > 0 is essential both to construct the reference index 0 : Fin N and to ensure the real reciprocal of N is nonzero.
The conclusion uses exact real equality and the coefficient is the real inverse of the cast of N.
MemLp and distributional assertions are measure-theoretic and therefore insensitive to suitable almost-everywhere changes, while the displayed average is defined pointwise before variance is applied.
For N = 1, the pairwise-independence hypothesis has no nontrivial instances and the conclusion reduces to variance(X 0) = variance(X 0).

For N greater than 1, the precise Mathlib notion of independence under a merely finite, non-probability measure may impose strong normalization or degeneracy constraints; the target does not state these consequences explicitly.
ambiguities: The packet does not specify whether μ is intended semantically as a probability measure despite providing only IsFiniteMeasure μ.
The one-level body of ProbabilityTheory.variance shows conversion from evariance but does not expose the full normalization convention of evariance.
The one-level body of IdentDistrib is unavailable because it is inductive, so its bundled measurability fields and exact equality formulation are not displayed.

The intended reading is the standard variance-of-an-i.i.d.-sample-mean identity, although the formal assumptions state pairwise independence and identical distribution separately rather than using an i.i.d. predicate.
